items.stem: According to WHO/UNICEF (2022), approximately how many people lacked safely managed drinking water?
items.answer: About 2.2 billion
items.markingKey: About 2.2 billion. About 3.5 billion lacked safely managed sanitation.

items.stem: The volume of water stored in a reservoir in Spain was 603 million m³ in 2005 and 649 million m³ in 2020. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (649 − 603) ÷ 603 × 100; A1 +7.6% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Explain the difference between a point bar and a river cliff.
items.answer: A river cliff is a steep erosional bank on the outside of a meander; a point bar is a gentle depositional slope of sand and gravel on the inside.
items.markingKey: A river cliff is a steep erosional bank on the outside of a meander; a point bar is a gentle depositional slope of sand and gravel on the inside. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Using Mexico City as an example, explain land subsidence from aquifer over-use.
items.answer: Groundwater pumping supplies a large share of the city's water and parts of the city are sinking by up to about 35-50 cm a year. Over-extraction compacts lake-bed clays, damaging buildings and pipes.
items.markingKey: Context (Groundwater pumping supplies a large share of the city's water and parts of the city are sinking by up to about 35-50 cm a year.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Over-extraction compacts lake-bed clays, damaging buildings and pipes. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to land subsidence from aquifer over-use.

items.stem: Examine the view that human activity now has a greater influence on drainage basin systems than physical factors.
items.answer: Human activity dominates in heavily used basins, but physical factors still set the framework.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - for: urbanisation, deforestation and dams alter flows (Amazon, Yangtze); irrigation and abstraction remove large volumes. Against / limitations: climate, geology and relief remain the basic controls; many remote basins are little modified. A supported conclusion might be: Human activity dominates in heavily used basins, but physical factors still set the framework. items.answer: A city that meets the needs of its present residents without compromising future generations, balancing environmental, social and economic goals

items.stem: Lukas writes: "All residents of informal settlements are unemployed." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Most residents work, often in the informal sector, and many settlements are economically productive (e.g. Dharavi).

items.stem: Using the regeneration of the London Docklands as an example, explain reurbanisation and regeneration.
items.answer: The LDDC (1981-1998) regenerated derelict docks; Canary Wharf now employs over 100,000 people. Investment brought new jobs and residents into a declining inner area, though many original residents felt excluded.
items.markingKey: Context (The LDDC (1981-1998) regenerated derelict docks; Canary Wharf now employs over 100,000 people.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem:
A student recorded the following data for a sample of countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America (site: female mean years of schooling, total fertility rate).
A: 12.4, 1.5; B: 10.3, 2.3; C: 12.2, 1.3; D: 5.3, 4.7; E: 1.2, 6.6; F: 7.4, 3.5; G: 9.6, 2.9; H: 3.3, 5.8; I: 1.9, 6.2; J: 3.6, 5.6.
Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rs = 1 − 6Σd² / (n³ − n)) and state whether the relationship is significant at the 0.05 level (one-tailed test; critical value for n = 10: 0.564). Suggest one geographical reason for the relationship and one limitation of the data.
items.answer: Σd² = 328; rs = 1 − 6×328/(10³ − 10) = -0.988; a negative correlation that is significant at the 0.05 level.

items.stem: Explain the difference between sudden-onset climate impacts and slow-onset climate impacts.
items.answer: Slow-onset impacts (sea-level rise, desertification, glacier retreat) build over years and lead to gradual migration; sudden-onset events (floods, cyclones) cause rapid, often temporary displacement.
items.markingKey: Slow-onset impacts (sea-level rise, desertification, glacier retreat) build over years and lead to gradual migration; sudden-onset events (floods, cyclones) cause rapid, often temporary displacement. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "Geo-engineering would solve climate change, so emissions cuts are unnecessary." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Solar geo-engineering would mask warming but not remove CO₂, leaving ocean acidification and the risk of rapid warming if it stopped.
items.markingKey: Solar geo-engineering would mask warming but not remove CO₂, leaving ocean acidification and the risk of rapid warming if it stopped. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why the growth of the global middle class increases resource consumption.
items.answer: Higher incomes are spent on meat and dairy (more land and water), cars and air travel (oil), larger homes, appliances and air-conditioning (electricity) and consumer goods (minerals), so per-capita demand rises sharply. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Higher incomes are spent on meat and dairy (more land and water), cars and air travel (oil), larger homes, appliances and air-conditioning (electricity) and consumer goods (minerals), so per-capita demand rises sharply. items.stem: "The Sustainable Development Goals are too ambitious to be achieved." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: The SDGs will not all be met by 2030, but they are valuable as a framework that directs action.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why progress towards the SDGs has been uneven.
items.answer: Countries differ in income, governance and conflict; shocks such as COVID-19, war in Ukraine and climate disasters reversed gains; funding gaps are large (trillions of dollars a year). (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Countries differ in income, governance and conflict; shocks such as COVID-19, war in Ukraine and climate disasters reversed gains; funding gaps are large (trillions of dollars a year). (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (4 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Noah writes: "Fertility falls only when countries become rich." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Kerala and Bangladesh reduced fertility to around replacement with low incomes through female education, health care and family planning.
items.markingKey: Kerala and Bangladesh reduced fertility to around replacement with low incomes through female education, health care and family planning. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why most Canadians live close to the border with the USA.
items.answer: About 90% live within about 160 km of the US border, where the climate is milder, the growing season longer, soils better and trade links with the USA strongest; the north is cold, has permafrost and is remote.

(4 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:
Study the infographic / visual stimulus described below.

Table: EU natural gas imports by supplier (% share) - 2021: Russia 40, Norway 23, USA (LNG) 6, Algeria 11, others 20; 2023: Russia 15, Norway 30, USA (LNG) 19, Algeria 12, others 24.

(a) Describe the change in the EU's gas suppliers between 2021 and 2023. [4]
(b) Using the resource and your own knowledge, explain how the change affects EU energy security. [6]
items.answer: (a) Russia's share fell from 40% to 15%; Norway (23 → 30%) and US LNG (6 → 19%) replaced much of it; supply became more diversified. (b) Less dependence on a hostile supplier reduces political risk, but LNG is more expensive and exposed to global market competition.
items.markingKey: (a) Russia's share fell from 40% to 15%; Norway (23 → 30%) and US LNG (6 → 19%) replaced much of it; supply became more diversified. (b) Less dependence on a hostile supplier reduces political risk, but LNG is more expensive and exposed to global market competition. Credit relevant own knowledge and named examples in (b). Infographic markscheme [10]: part (a) [4] - award 1 mark per valid point taken from the resource (data must be quoted with units for full marks); part (b) [6] - up to 2 marks for each developed explanation linking the resource to own knowledge; reward named examples; maximum 3 marks if the resource is not used.

items.stem: "Adaptation is a more urgent priority than mitigation for low-income countries." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: For low-income countries adaptation is the immediate priority, but it depends on global mitigation to remain feasible.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - arguments supporting the statement: impacts are already occurring and these countries emit little; adaptation saves lives immediately (Bangladesh cyclone shelters). Arguments challenging it: without global mitigation, adaptation limits will be exceeded (small islands); low-carbon development brings co-benefits and finance. Evaluation should weigh places, scales, perspectives and time. Judgement: For low-income countries adaptation is the immediate priority, but it depends on global mitigation to remain feasible. Paper 2 Section C markbands [15]: 13-15 thorough response to all demands including the command term; accurate, detailed geographical knowledge and terminology; well-chosen, located and quantified examples at more than one scale; explicit, balanced evaluation (perspectives, places, scales, time) with a well-substantiated conclusion. 10-12 most demands addressed; accurate knowledge; examples relevant and developed; evaluation is balanced but not sustained. 7-9 some demands addressed; knowledge mostly accurate; examples partly developed; evaluation partial or one-sided. 4-6 limited, mainly descriptive; generalised examples; little evaluation. 1-3 little relevant knowledge; no examples or evaluation. 0 does not reach the standard of the descriptors.
